record.paper_title: Problems in Data Structures and Algorithms
record.original_question: For binary search tree access sequences, does there exist any online update algorithm—not necessarily splaying—whose total cost is always within a constant factor of the optimum offline algorithm that knows the full future access sequence in advance?

evidence.quote: A weaker form of Problem 4.4 asks whether there is any on-line algorithm whose performance is within a constant factor of that of the optimum off-line algorithm.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the binary search tree (BST) model of computation. A BST stores a set of n keys and serves an access sequence x_1, x_2, ..., x_m of keys. To serve a request x_i, an algorithm starts at the root and follows a path of pointers; after locating x_i it may perform an arbitrary sequence of rotations in the tree. The cost of serving the request is the number of nodes touched (length of the search path plus the number of rotations performed).

An online BST algorithm decides its actions on request x_i using only knowledge of x_1, ..., x_i. An offline BST algorithm may use full knowledge of the entire request sequence in advance. For an access sequence σ, let OPT(σ) denote the minimum total cost achievable by any (offline) BST algorithm serving σ starting from some initial tree.

Question: Does there exist an online BST algorithm A and a constant c > 0 such that for every n, every initial BST on n keys, and every access sequence σ of keys, the total cost incurred by A on σ is at most c · OPT(σ) + O(m + n)?

Equivalently: is there any O(1)-competitive online BST algorithm (not necessarily based on splaying)?
artifact.status_search_result: The dynamic optimality conjecture and its weaker form asking for any O(1)-competitive online BST algorithm remain open as of 2024. The best known online algorithms (e.g., Tango trees, Multi-splay, Greedy/Demaine et al.) achieve O(log log n)-competitiveness, but no constant-competitive online BST algorithm is known. Recent 2024 work (e.g., ISAAC 2024 hardness amplification, ICALP 2024 group access bounds) continues to make partial progress without resolving the conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Splay tree - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Currently neither splay trees nor any other tree algorithm is known to be dynamically optimal.
status_evidence.claim: No known BST algorithm is proven O(1)-competitive.

status_evidence.title: Hardness Amplification for Dynamic Binary Search Trees (ISAAC 2024)
status_evidence.snippet: Direct-sum theorems for Wilber's lower bounds in the BST model.
status_evidence.claim: Active 2024 research on the still-unresolved dynamic optimality question.

status_evidence.title: The Group Access Bounds for Binary Search Trees (ICALP 2024)
status_evidence.snippet: New direction towards proving o(log n)-competitiveness of Splay and Greedy.
status_evidence.claim: Constant competitiveness is still an open target.
